questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate, who took the title of Bahman Shah after his accession to the throne?

questions.question: Valabhi, a city of ancient India was the capital of the _______ dynasty from the 5th to 8th Century CE.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maitraka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maitraka dynasty ruled in the western part of India, primarily the region of present-day Gujarat.
 
• Valabhi, the capital city of the Maitraka dynasty, was an important cultural and educational center during their reign.
 
• The dynasty was founded by Senapati Bhatarka, a former Gupta Empire military commander, around the middle of the 5th century CE.
 
• The Maitrakas were patrons of Buddhism and Jainism, and Valabhi was known for its Buddhist monasteries and Jain temples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valabhi**

 
 
• Valabhi was an ancient city located in the present-day Bhavnagar district of Gujarat, India.
 
• It served as the capital of the Maitraka dynasty from the 5th to the 8th century CE.
 
• Valabhi was renowned as a center of learning and attracted scholars from various parts of India.
 
• The city was known for its educational institutions, particularly Buddhist monasteries, which were comparable to those at Nalanda.
 
 
 
• **Maitraka Dynasty**
 
 
• The Maitraka dynasty was founded by Senapati Bhatarka, a former military governor of the Gupta Empire.
 
• They ruled primarily over the Saurashtra region of Gujarat from the 5th to the 8th century CE.
 
• The Maitrakas played a significant role in the cultural and religious development of western India.
 
• The dynasty came to an end in the mid-8th century CE, likely due to Arab invasions and internal strife.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire that existed from approximately 320 to 550 CE.
 
• Founded by Maharaja Sri Gupta, the empire is known for its achievements in the arts, architecture, sciences, religion, and philosophy.
 
• The period of the Gupta Empire is often referred to as the Golden Age of India due to the extensive cultural developments and prosperity.
 
• The Gupta rulers supported Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, fostering a diverse cultural and religious landscape.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism and Jainism**
 
 
• Buddhism is a major world religion founded by Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, in the 5th century BCE in India.
 
• Buddhism emphasizes the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path as a way to achieve enlightenment and end suffering.
 
• Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that teaches non-violence, truth, and asceticism.
 
• Founded by Mahavira in the 6th century BCE, Jainism emphasizes the principles of non-attachment and self-discipline.

questions.question: In which of the following battles did Muhammad of Ghor defeat Jayachandra of Gahadavala dynasty in 1194 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Chandawar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Chandawar took place in 1194 AD between Muhammad of Ghor and Jayachandra of the Gahadavala dynasty.
 
• This battle marked the defeat of Jayachandra, leading to the expansion of Muhammad of Ghor’s empire in Northern India.
 
• Jayachandra was a prominent ruler of the Gahadavala dynasty, which ruled parts of present-day Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• The defeat of Jayachandra significantly weakened the Gahadavala dynasty and paved the way for further Muslim conquests in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Battle of Tarain (1191)**

 
 
• The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 between Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad of Ghor.
 
• Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad of Ghor in this battle.
 
• This battle took place near the town of Tarain (modern Taraori) in Haryana, India.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Anhilwara (1178)**
 
 
• The Battle of Anhilwara was fought in 1178 between the Solanki king Mularaja II and Muhammad of Ghor.
 
• Mularaja II defeated Muhammad of Ghor in this battle.
 
• This battle took place at Anhilwara (modern Patan) in Gujarat, India.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Tarain (1192)**
 
 
• The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 between Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad of Ghor.
 
• Muhammad of Ghor defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in this decisive battle.
 
• This victory paved the way for the establishment of Muslim rule in Northern India.
 
 
 
• **Gahadavala Dynasty**
 
 
• The Gahadavala dynasty ruled parts of North India, primarily in the regions of present-day Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• They are known for their resistance against the Muslim invasions during the 12th century.
 
• Jayachandra, also known as Jaichand, was one of the most famous rulers of this dynasty.

questions.question: Which of the following is a work on statecraft written by Krishnadevaraya?

__
 
• Krishnadevaraya, the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara, composed a work on statecraft in Telugu **known as the Amuktamalyada. **

 
 
• **About traders he wrote :**

 
 
• A king should improve the harbors of his country and so encourage its commerce that horses, elephants, precious gems, sandalwood, pearls, and other articles are freely imported.
 
 
 
• He should sailors who land in his country on account of storms, illness and exhaustion are looked after in a suitable manner.
 
• **Amuktamalyada** describes the story of the wedding of the Hindu Lord Ranganayaka an avatar of Vishnu and Goda Devi aka Andal the Tamil Alvar poet and daughter of Periyalvar, at Srirangam.
 
• **Krishnadevaraya was the king of the Vijayanagara Empire reigning between 1509–1530.**
 
• He was the third ruler of the Tuluva Dynasty and presided over the Vijayanagara empire at its zenith. 
 
• Krishnadevaraya built huge irrigation tanks and reservoirs for harvesting rainwater.
 
• He distributed the wealth he gained in wars to all major temples of South India for the purpose of constructing temple gateways (gopura), called 'Rayagopuram,' in his honour.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Vijayanagara or “city of victory” was the name of both a city and an empire.
 
• The empire was **founded** in the fourteenth century (1336 AD) by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.
 
• **They made Hampi the capital city. **

questions.question: Which of the following systems of the Delhi sultanate influenced the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iqtadari**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Iqtadari System**:

__
 
• The Iqtadari system was a significant administrative and revenue collection system employed by the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Under this system, territories were divided into administrative units known as Iqta'at, and these units were granted to officials called Iqtadars.
 
• The Iqtadars were responsible for collecting taxes and revenue from their assigned territories and forwarding a portion of the collected revenue to the central authority.
 
• The Iqtadars held both administrative and fiscal authority in their assigned regions.

**Influence on Bahmani Sultanate**:

 
• The Bahmani Sultanate was established in the Deccan region as an independent kingdom after the disintegration of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• The Iqtadari system's influence extended to the Bahmani Sultanate, as it adopted similar administrative practices to manage its territories.
 
• While not an exact replication, the Bahmani rulers implemented a system of revenue collection and administration that was reminiscent of the Iqtadari system.
 
• This helped them organize and manage their vast and diverse territories efficiently.

**Influence on Vijayanagara Empire**:

 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was another significant medieval South Indian kingdom that coexisted with the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• While geographically separated from the Delhi Sultanate, the Iqtadari system indirectly influenced the Vijayanagara Empire's administrative and revenue collection practices.
 
• The Vijayanagara rulers, like their counterparts in the Deccan, implemented an administrative structure that involved the collection of revenue from various regions under their control.
 
• Although not a direct adoption, the idea of revenue collection and administrative divisions in the Iqtadari system influenced the governance model of the Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was sacked by victorious armies after the battle of Talikota?

• The victorious armies of the Deccan Sultanates, comprising **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Bidar,** and **Golconda,** sacked the city of **Vijayanagar **after winning the battle.

questions.question: The 'Pattanulkars' migrated from the Gujarat region to the Vijayanagar state. They were _________.
